key_insight: DAWG combines belief-propagation ensembles with graph sparsification to achieve competitive quantum error-correction decoding while reducing reliance on post-processing.
engineering_relevance: Fewer post-processing calls and a smaller post-processing graph could reduce decoding latency tails and specialized-hardware resource requirements.
method: Run serial minimum-sum belief propagation on the full detector error model Tanner graph, then continue on a sparsified graph.
Diversify ensemble members using distinct posterior-transfer matrices and randomized update schedules.
Combine DAWG with order-0 Localized Statistics Decoding (LSD-0) post-processing.
evidence_signal: Numerical studies on bivariate bicycle codes and superdense color-code circuits report performance similar to Relay BP and Vibe with LSD-0, with roughly tenfold fewer post-processing calls than Vibe at the same ensemble size.
watch_item: Real-time latency and hardware savings remain to be demonstrated in implementation; fewer post-processing calls alone do not establish end-to-end speed.
paper_title: Decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification for quantum low-density parity-check codes
